stories.title: Blackstone CEO bankrolls ad attacking Democrat for buying Blackstone stock
stories.text: At President Trump’s urging, the Florida legislature redrew the state’s electoral maps in an effort to increase the number of Republicans in Florida’s Congressional delegation. One of the members targeted by the changes is Congresswoman Kathy Castor (D-FL), who represents the state’s 14th Congressional District. Republicans changed the borders of Castor’s district in May 2026. The new 14th Congressional District supported Trump over Harris by more than 10 points. In an election where Republicans are facing political headwinds, flipping Castor’s seat is a top priority. No Going Back PAC, an offshoot of Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC, has spent at least $6.4 million opposing Castor. About $2.4 million of No Going Back PAC’s spending, according to AdImpact, has gone toward broadcasting an ad that attacks Castor for buying stock in a financial company that bought up property in Tampa. “In Congress, Kathy Castor traded stocks in a Wall Street firm that bought more than 1,600 Tampa Bay homes, raising rents and pricing people out,” the narrator says. “Kathy Castor profited.” Although the ad does not name the “Wall Street firm,” it cites a June 22, 2013, article published in the Tampa Bay Tim

stories.title: Hegseth Honors Terrorist With Firing Squad Gift
stories.text: Not accepting a dime in corporate ad money allows me to be genuinely independent; but it also means I’m ENTIRELY dependent on readers like you to survive. Nidal Hasan, the Army soldier who killed 13 fellow troops at Fort Hood in 2009, will still be shot to death by Army riflemen on December 3. “Death penalty through firing squad, and he deserves it,” Donald Trump said of Hasan earlier this month. He doesn’t deserve it — but not for the reasons you might expect. Execution by firing squad is regarded as a “soldier’s death,” long considered an honorable end and part of a military tradition that separates those who served from mere criminals. That’s why leaders from Nazi Germany to Saddam Hussein sought to die by firing squad, and why they were always denied. That Pete Hegseth, a former Army Major obsessed with restoring the military’s “warrior ethos,” does not know this is outrageous. It is also a gift to Nidal Hasan, who has been remarkably clear about his desire to be seen as and treated like a soldier. That is, a soldier for Allah (as he refers to himself). stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Lindsay Owens: Who Is Your AI Shopping Agent Working For?
stories.text: David Sirota talks with Lindsay Owens, president and CEO of Groundwork Collaborative and author of Gouged: The End of a Fair Price and What That Means for Your Wallet , about how companies use your data to decide what you pay. Owens argues that after 150 years, the price tag is “at risk of extinction,” as companies shift from pricing based on cost to pricing based on what each shopper will tolerate. She points to the Instacart experiment her group exposed, which found shoppers paying up to 23 percent more for the same item at the same time. They also dig into the next frontier: AI shopping agents. Owens describes research in which assistants told to find the cheapest option sometimes returned pricier ones after pulling in personal data, and she says shoppers deserve to know whether their agent works for them or for the highest bidder. Her main fix is a ban on using personal data to set prices. New York’s legislature has passed one, and Gov. Kathy Hochul has until the end of the year to sign it. stories.title: Why Are Democrats The Party Of No?
stories.text: It is an open secret that establishment Democrats loathe the left of their own party more than they oppose Republicans. You can see it in corporate Democrats trying to sabotage populist Democratic nominees and vilifying the Democratic Socialists of America. Less well understood is a related dynamic: Establishment Democrats’ foremost mission — the thing they equate with the ultimate form of toughness, courage, and morality — is using power to block the full set of policies the public actually wants. To them, Democrats’ highest virtue is not their ability to enact big ideas, but instead their willingness to replace the GOP as the new party of no and be this era’s William Buckley — a bulwark that “stands athwart history, yelling stop, at a time when no one is inclined to do so, or to have much patience with those who so urge it.” This vector isn’t much talked about in polite circles, but it is finally getting a rare moment in the sun, after a series of scream-the-quiet-part spectacles related to Medicare For All, which a new Yale study shows could save $1 trillion and 114,000 lives every year. stories.title: The Mystery Voter Guide Using Democrats To Elect Mike Rogers
stories.text: This is a web version of The Lever ’s daily email newsletter. Copies of an “anti-extremism voters guide” promoting Republican Senate hopeful Mike Rogers alongside state Democratic candidates were apparently distributed to homes in Michigan without most of those Democrats’ knowledge. The pamphlet carries the insignia of Beacon Coalition, a Jewish-American political nonprofit that recently endorsed Rogers and has received funding from the center-left dark-money powerhouse Third Way. According to a photo recently shared on social media, the “anti-extremism” pamphlets encourage voters to elect a bipartisan slate of “pro-democracy” candidates composed of four state Democrats and two Republicans, including Rogers. Conspicuously snubbed is Rogers’ opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed. The GOP has widely attempted to smear El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as an extremist , framing his potent criticism of Israel as religious radicalism and antisemitism. “I’m not here to defend myself. stories.title: Angie Nixon's Formula For Winning Without Corporate Cash
stories.text: Americans are paying more for groceries and fighting their insurance companies for medical care while their taxes subsidize Elon Musk’s companies and Walmart’s low wages. Democrats are promising to fight back, but many in the party still accept corporate cash, and some argue that democratic socialists can’t beat Republicans. Can a populist candidate who refuses corporate PAC money win in a red state? We’re about to find out. In this exclusive, uncut interview for our premium subscribers, Lever columnist Morgan Harper speaks with Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon, the Democratic Senate nominee and an outspoken member of the Democratic Socialists of America. Nixon is running against Sen. Ashley Moody (R-Fla.), Gov. Ron DeSantis’ hand-picked appointee. Nixon tells us why she called out a corporate sponsor at this year’s Congressional Black Caucus Foundation conference, what’s fueling the racist attacks on her campaign, and how the Black Panther Party influenced her organizing — including the free Plan B pills she gives away at her bookstore and coffee shop.
